chunks.text:
Montelukast helps to reduce inflammation.
It may be used to prevent asthma attacks in adults and children at least 2 years old.
Montelukast is used to prevent exercise-induced bronchoconstriction.
Exercise-induced bronchoconstriction is a narrowing of the air passages in the lungs due to exercise.
It is also known as exercise-induced asthma.
Montelukast is used in adults and children who are at least 6 years old.
Montelukast may be considered for adults and children at least 2 years old with symptoms of seasonal allergic rhinitis.
Montelukast may be considered for people over 6 months old with perennial (year-round) allergies.
This consideration applies when other treatments have not worked.
If you already take montelukast regularly to prevent asthma or allergy symptoms.
Do not take an extra dose.
Do not take an extra dose to treat exercise-induced bronchoconstriction.
Montelukast is not a fast-acting rescue medicine for asthma attacks.
It needs to be taken daily to work properly.
Montelukast was FDA-approved in 1998.

Tell your doctor if you have ever had:

Seek medical attention if your breathing problems get worse quickly, or if you think your medications are not working.
Montelukast is usually taken once every evening, with or without food.
For exercise-induced bronchoconstriction, take a single dose at least 2 hours before exercise.
Do not take another dose for at least 24 hours.
Swallow the regular tablet whole, with a glass of water.
You must chew the chewable tablet before you swallow it.
Place the oral granules directly in your mouth and swallow.
You can mix oral granules with applesauce, mashed carrots, rice, or ice cream.
The granules may also be mixed with baby formula or breast milk.
Do not use any other type of liquid.
Use the mixture within 15 minutes.
Do not save for later use.
You should not stop using oral steroid medication suddenly.
This applies if you also use an oral steroid medication.

Use your next dose at the regular time.

chunks.section_heading: What should I avoid while taking montelukast?
chunks.text:
Avoid situations or activities that may trigger an asthma attack.
If your asthma symptoms get worse when you take aspirin, avoid taking aspirin.
Avoid taking other NSAIDs (nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs).
Examples of NSAIDs include ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin), naproxen (Aleve), celecoxib, diclofenac, indomethacin, meloxicam, and others.

Signs of an allergic reaction to montelukast include hives, blisters, and severe itching.
Signs of an allergic reaction to montelukast also include difficult breathing.
Signs of an allergic reaction to montelukast also include swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat.

agitation, aggression, feeling restless or irritable;
